cases.title: Check a whole authored post against a literal policy
cases.description: One fixed saved document and ordered dictionary. No rotation or averaging across different inputs.

documents.text:
We are trying to understand why the parcel tracker and the order page disagree. The parcel contains a monitor arm and a small adapter for our meeting room. The warehouse marked both items as packed on Monday, but the courier history shows a collection scan for only one box. There is no damage report or failed delivery attempt in the tracking history. We have checked the delivery address against the invoice and it is correct.

The first box arrived yesterday. Its label lists one package out of two, and the adapter was inside. The monitor arm is still missing. The receptionist checked the loading area and the cabinet where parcels are stored overnight. Nobody has signed for a second box, and the building camera shows only one delivery from that courier. We have kept the packaging and can provide photographs of the label if they help identify the shipment.

Please ask the warehouse whether the second item received a separate tracking number. We do not need a replacement adapter, and we would rather avoid opening two unrelated tickets for the same order. If the arm has not left the warehouse, let us know the revised dispatch date. If it is already with the courier, a reference that identifies the missing box would let the reception team follow the correct delivery. The meeting room installation is scheduled for next week, so we can wait a few days if we have a clear update.

dictionary_source.extraction: Eight canonical entry IDs, then literal alternatives split on | with regex operators/escapes excluded. Remaining entries are in deterministic SHA256 order. Case preserved. Source exceptions, wildcards and word-boundary policies are not implemented: this fixture tests exact byte matching only.
dictionary_source.selection: 16 project-authored promotional phrases, followed by the first 112 terms of the pinned literal extraction, in saved order.
dictionary_source.literal_policy: No boundaries, exceptions, normalization or case folding; this is a byte prefilter fixture.
